habitat: Secretive pairs in dense coastal and valley bush, lowland forest fringes, riverine forest and mixed bushveld, in the lower stratum, searching for insects.
summary: A fairly common resident. The male has a scarlet throat and a black gorget. The female is similar but the black gorget is much reduced. The colour line also gives a yellow belly. Newman does not describe the upperparts, and the immature is only shown. The call is a liquid, ventriloquial kong-kong-koit. Newman’s page uses Chlorophoneus viridis. The stored name Telophorus viridis was left unchanged. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Upperpart colour is not described, and the immature is only illustrated, which is why this needs review. The Newman page uses Chlorophoneus viridis. This file keeps Telophorus viridis. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
